notes:
Session context dump for T634 (per-harness liveness fuse). Raw evidence behind findings/T634-liveness-fuse.json.

## (1) The defect, with the two readings side by side
The startup-liveness fuse (T586) keyed on stdout: 'startup liveness timeout 600s (10'00) — agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)'. Its premise — silence means a stalled worker — is true for a pi lane (streams via --mode json) and FALSE for a claude lane (headless `claude -p` buffers its output to the end). Two lanes ran the same brief minutes apart:
- T615 (claude-fable-5): wall 598.8 s, exit 0, delivered, closed pass.
- T616 (claude-opus-5): wall 600.8 s, killed, recorded verified=fail fail=row.
T616 had already written findings/T616-race-f.json (43 KB, 33 adjudicated union items, every `real` verdict cited) when the fuse killed it for being quiet. Two seconds separated a pass from a failure, and the bias is not random: a 600 s stdout fuse penalises exactly the larger/thorough models that take longer.

## (2) The sensor chosen, and why
For claude lanes the liveness sensor is mtime movement on (a) the DECLARED DELIVERABLES (the bundle's `deliverables=` header, resolved against repo_root) and (b) the CLAUDE SESSION TRANSCRIPT (~/.claude/projects/<project_slug(cwd)>/, including one level of per-session subdirectories). A working claude lane appends to its session .jsonl on every assistant turn and every tool call, so its transcript mtime moves continuously (seconds-to-minutes); the declared deliverables move as the lane edits its output files. Both are attributable to the lane.

The shared repo tree is deliberately NOT a sensor: other consoles write to the same checkout, so a neighbour's edit would mark a hung lane 'alive' — noise defeats the fuse. That is the honest 'scratch area' answer: the transcript directory IS the per-lane scratch (the harness's own working log); the shared working tree is not scannable per-lane.

What a genuinely hung claude lane looks like under this sensor: its transcript mtime flatlines (no tool calls, no assistant turns — the harness is stalled or dead) and no deliverable mtime moves. That is distinguishable from a working lane, whose transcript max-mtime keeps advancing. The sensor can distinguish the two; a hung lane is killed for 'liveness timeout ... no mtime movement'.

## (3) Threshold derivation (derived, not guessed)
Computed from untracked/runs/*.json `wall`, per family (completed runs carrying a wall reading), snapshot 2026-08-22:
- claude: n=29, p95 (linear interpolation) = 1543.5 s, 3x = 4630.4 s -> default --claude-liveness-timeout = 4631 s (ceil). Nearest-rank p95 = 1754.6 s (index 27) for transparency; 3x of that = 5263.8 s, so 4631 s is the conservative (lower) derived figure.
- deepseek (pi): n=113, p95 = 2340.9 s.
- ollama: n=9, p95 = 2255.0 s.
- other (non-agent builds): n=22, p95 = 145.2 s.
A constant with no denominator is what produced 600 s; 4631 s = 3 x the observed p95 of the claude family it governs.

## (4) T629 coordination (fuse kill unscoreable)
T629 (killed_by schema) is BLOCKED (needs T631) at write time, so I emit the reason on the run record in the shape T629 must key on: run record carries kill_class="liveness" (mirroring the existing kill_class="directive" pattern) plus a `killed` string — 'liveness timeout <n>s (...) — claude lane showed no mtime movement...' for the claude fuse, and the T586-identical 'startup liveness timeout ...' for the pi/ollama fuse, now also marked kill_class="liveness". T629 must map kill_class=="liveness" (or killed.startswith("liveness")/startswith("startup liveness")) to killed_by="liveness", and refuse to score any such row. The stderr message for the pi path is byte-identical to T586's (null control: same timing, same message).

## (5) Red (pre-fix) and green (post-fix)
RED, against HEAD (pre-T634) tools/runner, replaying T616's shape with a claude-named stub that writes its deliverable and appends to its transcript while emitting NO stdout/stderr for 5 s (> the old --startup-timeout 2 s):
  [runner] startup liveness: agent lane, timeout 2s
  [runner] KILL: startup liveness timeout 2s (2s) — agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)
  [runner] exit 124 (startup liveness timeout 2s (2s) — agent lane produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)) in 4.5 s
  -> exit 124; the lane was writing work (deliverable on disk, transcript appended each second) and was killed for being quiet. This is the exact T616 defect shape.
GREEN, against the fixed runner, same fixture: exit 0, deliverable on disk, no liveness fuse fired ('survives' arm of tools/regression-runner-claude-liveness.sh).

HUNG (seeded): claude-named stub, no stdout AND no mtime movement anywhere -> killed at --claude-liveness-timeout with 'liveness timeout' + exit 124, run record kill_class="liveness".
NULL: pi lane stalls -> killed exactly as today (tools/regression-runner-startup-liveness.sh stays green — red/green/scoping arms all pass); fast claude lane (deliverable written immediately) -> untouched.

## (6) T615/T616 margins under the new threshold
Threshold 4631 s. T616 (600.8 s): survives by 4030.2 s. T615 (598.8 s): survives by 4032.2 s. Both would have been allowed to finish; neither approaches the fuse.
